title: Predictive biomarkers for immunotherapy response
bottleneck: No reliable biomarker predicts who will benefit from checkpoint inhibitors: PD-L1 staining, tumor mutational burden, and microsatellite instability each identify only subsets of responders, and many biomarker-negative patients respond while biomarker-positive patients do not.
why_it_blocks: Without prediction, patients endure costly, toxic therapies with low odds of benefit, and trials enroll broad populations that dilute signals of efficacy.
current_state: Composite signatures combining genomic, transcriptomic, and microenvironment features are improving prediction, and dynamic on-treatment markers show promise. Research into microenvironment regulators such as the miR-25 pathway may yield new predictive markers, but a single robust test remains elusive. Liquid-biopsy-based dynamic markers that track immune activation during treatment may prove more predictive than any baseline test. Integrating these into routine care will require prospective validation.
